newsitem.title: USA: California wine grape crop seen at record.
newsitem.headline: California wine grape crop seen at record.

text.p: California wine grape production this year is estimated at a record 2.7 million tons, up 21 percent from last year, the California Department of Food and Agriculture said on Friday.
Farmers expected a good quality wine grape crop this year, it said in its July crop production estimates.

Production of table grapes this year was expected to be 700,000 tons, up 18 percent from 1996, it said. Raisin grape production this year, forecast at 2.4 million tons, was up 10 percent from last year, it said.
The 1997 apricot crop was estimated at 125,000 tons, up 64 percent from last year, the department said.
Freestone peach production this year was expected to be 380,000 tons, up 20 percent from last year, with a yield of 10.8 tons per acre, it said.
This year's Clingstone peach crop was forecast at 550,000 tons, up one percent from 1996, with a yield of 17.7 tons per acre, it said.
The 1997 lemon forecast was 44.0 million cartons, a five percent increase from last year's production level of 42.0 million cartons, the department said.
It said 1996/97 navel orange production was forecast at 86.0 million cartons, up 13 percent from last season. The fruit has excellent quality with very large fruit size, the department said.
The Valencia orange forecast, at 56.0 million cartons, was unchanged from last year, it said.
Grapefruit production for 1996/97 was forecast at 18.4 million cartons, 14 percent above last season, the department said.

Walnut production was forecast at 230,000 tons, up 11 percent from last year. Bearing acreage was estimated at 170,000 acres. This year's crop was larger than last year's because of increased Hartley production, it said.
The barley production forecast was down 11 percent at 280,800 tons. Oats production was forecast at 38,400 tons, up seven percent from last year.
Winter wheat production was forecast at 855,000 tons, down 25 percent from last year, and durum wheat production was forecast at 370,500 tons, down 11 percent from last year, the department said.
